    Restricted permutation designs

    Source: R/ordination-canoco.R
    ord_design.Rd

    Describes how sites may be shuffled in a permutation test when they are not independent, as the permutation options of CANOCO do. Give the result as design to ord_test(), ord_select() or ord_effects().

    • Blocks (blocks): sites are shuffled only within blocks, never between them. Use for randomised block designs; as in CANOCO, also add the blocks as covariables (+ Condition(block) in the formula).

    • Split-plot (plots): whole plots (groups of sites) are shuffled as units (plots_type), and the sites within each plot are shuffled (within) or kept in place (within = "none"). Use when a treatment is applied to whole plots.

    • Time series and transects (within = "series"): sites keep their order and are shifted cyclically, which keeps temporal or spatial autocorrelation intact.

    • Rectangular grids (within = "grid", with nrow and ncol): toroidal shifts of a grid of sites.

    Sites must be in the order the design describes (time, or the grid row by row), which is the order of the site column after sorting.

    Usage

    ord_design(
  blocks = NULL,
  plots = NULL,
  within = c("free", "series", "grid", "none"),
  plots_type = c("none", "free", "series", "grid"),
  nrow = NULL,
  ncol = NULL,
  mirror = FALSE
)

    Arguments

    blocks

    Name of the site variable defining blocks.

    plots

    Name of the site variable defining whole plots.

    within

    How sites are shuffled within plots (or within blocks, or overall): "free", "series", "grid" or "none".

    plots_type

    How whole plots are shuffled: "none" (kept in place), "free", "series" or "grid".

    nrow, ncol

    Grid dimensions for "grid".

    mirror

    Also use mirror images of series and grids.

    Value

    A td_design object.

    References

    Leps, J. and Smilauer, P. (2003). Multivariate Analysis of Ecological Data using CANOCO. Cambridge University Press. Chapter 5.

    Simpson, G. L. (2022). permute: Functions for Generating Restricted Permutations of Data. R package.

    Examples

    d <- community_long(dune_species, cols = -site)
o <- ord_fit(d, abundance = abundance, method = "rda", formula = ~ A1,
  env = dune_env, permutations = 0)
# shuffle sites only within management types
ord_test(o, permutations = 199, design = ord_design(blocks = "Management"))
#> # A tibble: 2 × 5
#>   term        df variance statistic p.value
#>   <chr>    <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>   <dbl>
#> 1 Model        1   0.0722      2.68     0.1
#> 2 Residual    18   0.484      NA       NA
